clue.text: Explain advantage of the dole

parts.note: to state a case is to set it out or explain it
a benefit is an advantage or gain

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the good side of being on the dole is.
explanation.definitionFit: The dole is the British colloquial name for unemployment pay, a welfare payment from government.

clue.text: Southern fatso the first to leap in making a big splash

indicators.note: in tells us the opening letter goes inside the word for a fat person

parts.note: podge is an informal word for a fat person

indicators.note: the first to signals taking only the opening letter of the following word leap

explanation.surface: A heavy southerner is first to jump into the pool and makes an enormous splash.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge is a large irregular blot or smear of colour or liquid.

clue.text: Origin of Adidas, for instance, is sponsorship

indicators.note: origin of means the start, so only the opening letter of Adidas is taken

parts.note: eg (exempli gratia) means for instance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a sportswear brand like Adidas is the essence of sports sponsorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the aegis of someone means under their protection or patronage, the backing a sponsor gives.

clue.text: A nerd gets hopelessly out of touch

indicators.note: hopelessly suggests a muddle, so the letters of a nerd gets are jumbled

explanation.surface: A geek drifts hopelessly away from reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone estranged has lost contact or become alienated from people they were close to.

clue.text: Essentially quiet nature of volatile mount

indicators.note: essentially here means at the core of, so the letters sit in the middle of quiet nature

explanation.surface: A paradox: a mountain whose essential character is calm is somehow volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the famously active volcano on Sicily, a mountain liable to erupt.

clue.text: Curious about one poem composed on Top Shop

indicators.note: in a down answer on top means the first part sits above the second
composed suggests the letters of poem are put together afresh
about means the word for curious wraps round the numeral

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An odd tale of a poem written about the high-street fashion chain Topshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Shop' reads as the British fashion chain Topshop, but 'on Top' only means the first piece stands above the second in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large store selling many kinds of goods.

clue.text: With cigarette end found in pint, turned awkward

indicators.note: found in says that closing letter is placed inside pint
turned signals the combined letters are rearranged
end picks out the closing letter of cigarette

explanation.surface: A drinker finds a cigarette butt in their beer and turns away in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts E inside PINT to give PINET, and 'turned' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill, as an awkward person is.

clue.text: Fussy 4/4 beat

indicators.note: beat in the sense of beaten or battered signals the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: 4/4 is read as the words four four

explanation.surface: A finicky drummer keeping strict common time.
explanation.walkthrough: '4/4' looks like a time signature but is spelt out as FOUR FOUR to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Frou-frou describes showy, frilly ornamentation, elaborate and over-decorated.

clue.text: Avenge suffering in UN location

indicators.note: suffering suggests something damaged, so the letters of avenge are disturbed

explanation.surface: A call for vengeance on behalf of victims, brought to a United Nations venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva in Switzerland hosts the European headquarters of the United Nations.

clue.text: Went inside, wreathed in smoke, to relax

indicators.note: wreathed in means those inner letters are surrounded by the phrase for smoke

parts.note: to light up is to start smoking a cigarette

indicators.note: inside means only the inner letters of the word went are used

explanation.surface: Someone goes indoors, surrounded by cigarette smoke, to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is to become less serious or tense, to ease off.

clue.text: Flat bitter? That is unusual

indicators.note: flat beer has lost its head, so the first letter of the drink goes

parts.note: bitter is a British type of beer
ie (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A pub-goer complains a flat pint of bitter is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a hoppy British draught ale; beer with no head is flat, hence EER.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, uncanny in an out-of-the-ordinary way.

clue.text: Sad, bad laddism not dead

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of laddism are corrupted into a new order
not means the abbreviation for dead is left out of the jumbled letters

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A comment that boorish laddish behaviour is depressing and refuses to die out.
explanation.walkthrough: Laddism is British slang for loutish young-male behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means gloomy and depressing, a synonym of sad.

clue.text: Stick out for diamonds in genuine setting

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: in says the card-suit letter goes inside the word for genuine
setting means the word for genuine acts as a mount around the gem letter

parts.note: true means genuine or real
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Supporting diamonds in an authentic jewellery setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to project beyond a surface, to jut out.

clue.text: Huge number in short turned out to be sufficient

indicators.note: turned out suggests reworking the letters of huge and the short form of number

parts.note: No is the shortened form of number

explanation.surface: A huge number, put briefly, proved to be plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough means adequate in quantity, as much as is needed.

clue.text: Hothouse Kid who played trombone without emotion

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the surname wraps round the emotion

parts.note: Kid Ory was a New Orleans jazz trombonist
anger is a strong emotion

explanation.surface: A jazz trombonist playing deadpan, with no feeling, in a greenhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glass-walled building for growing citrus trees, a kind of greenhouse.

clue.text: Hatred of European Union rule replacing British jubilation

indicators.note: replacing says one abbreviation takes the place of another in the word for hatred

parts.note: a phobia is an aversion or hatred

explanation.surface: A political observation: Europhobia gives way to Euro rule and wild celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is a feeling of intense happiness or elation.

clue.text: Why Enigma Variation writer isn't Elgar

indicators.note: variation suggests a changed form, so the letters of why enigma are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking why the composer of the Enigma Variations is not named Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enigma Variation' recalls Elgar's famous work; 'isn't Elgar' warns that the writer here is another man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist, author of The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: Glasses so restricted boxing adjudicator

indicators.note: boxing means the words glasses so restricted enclose the letters required

explanation.surface: A judge wearing glasses so tight they limit his view of a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates or judges, for example in an exam or legal case.

clue.text: Somewhat mild praise?

parts.note: bland means mild or unexciting
the suffix -ish means somewhat

explanation.surface: A query: is lukewarm praise really praise at all?
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax with flattery, to cajole with compliments.

clue.text: Old man housed in unfinished Denby development was warmer before retirement

indicators.note: housed in means the word for father sits within the rearranged letters
development suggests the remaining letters grow into a new arrangement
unfinished says the word Denby loses its last letter

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A father living in a half-built Denby housing estate kept warm before retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: Denby is a Derbyshire village and pottery maker. 'unfinished' trims it to DENB; 'development' rearranges that to BEDN, with PA inside. 'retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed pan was formerly a warming pan holding hot coals, passed through sheets before sleeping.

clue.text: Launch unexpected attack on leading hospital doctor in Australia

indicators.note: in means the medical letters go inside the abbreviation for Australia

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: leading means just the first letter of hospital

explanation.surface: A surprise assault on the top medic at a hospital in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambush is to surprise someone with an attack from a hidden position.

clue.text: Tough cowl on chimney

parts.note: a hood is a cowl, a covering for the head or a chimney top
lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney

explanation.surface: A description of a cowl fitted on top of a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough here is a noun meaning a thug, a violent ruffian or gangster.

clue.text: 'Snoop before loop' — beginner's second-rate poetry

parts.note: the rapper Snoop Dogg supplies the surname
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: beginner's means taking the first letter of loop

explanation.surface: A novice's dreadful verse that runs 'Snoop before loop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is comic or badly written verse with clumsy rhythm.

clue.text: Force out old performers

parts.note: ex means former, old
an act is a performer or group of performers in a show

explanation.surface: Driving out a troupe of ageing performers.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and extract something by force, such as payment.

clue.text: One doing wrong is blue

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of doing are set out incorrectly

explanation.surface: Someone who has done wrong feels depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a mood here, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep shade of blue between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Get unfit from being a member of a gym?

parts.note: in means belonging to, as when you are in a club
PT, physical training, is gym lessons at school

explanation.surface: A question whether joining a gym could somehow make you less fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate for a purpose.

clue.text: Spirit of almost entirely hollow braggadocio

indicators.note: almost entirely hollow means nearly all the inner letters of braggadocio are emptied out, leaving two at each end

explanation.surface: Boastful bluster that turns out to be nearly empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vigour, liveliness and spirited energy.

clue.text: Arterial route with a junction in unfinished road repair

indicators.note: in means the junction letter is placed inside those letters
repair suggests the remaining letters are fixed into a new order
unfinished says the word road loses its last letter

parts.note: a T-junction gives T

explanation.surface: Traffic news about a main road and a junction amid unfinished roadworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts road to ROA, and 'repair' rearranges that to ORA, with T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood from the heart, a route arterial in the literal sense.

clue.text: Starting first dance after eight, say, is daft

indicators.note: after says the dance comes behind the crew
first means just the opening letter of starting

parts.note: a rowing eight is an example of a crew
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Claiming that dancing first thing after eight o'clock is silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwball means eccentric or crazy, used of people and comedies.

clue.text: Some setters sloppily accepting 'the ultimate in technology' for 'hi-fi'

indicators.note: accepting means the jumbled letters take in another letter
sloppily means the letters of some setters are carelessly jumbled
the ultimate in means the last letter of technology

explanation.surface: Careless crossword setters accept a phrase as a definition of hi-fi.
explanation.definitionFit: A hi-fi is a high-fidelity sound system for playing recorded music.
